receipt.public_excerpt: In my study, I found only Canada and Brazil are drafting similar frameworks, and both of those initiatives remain mired in legislative limbo. The UK, Australia, New Zealand, Switzerland, Singapore, and Japan are taking a pro-innovation, less restrictive track on AI regulation.

evidence_items.explanation: A 2025 study found few countries copying the EU AI Act, and many major economies taking a lighter path. That cuts against 'much of the world' looking to Europe.

evidence_items.explanation: Vietnam passed an AI law on 10 December 2025 that follows the EU AI Act's risk-based model. Some countries did look to Europe in 2025.

receipt.public_excerpt: the Commission proposed to delay the EU’s stricter rules on the use of AI in a range of areas seen as more high risk, to December 2027 from August 2026.

unresolved_gaps: No systematic 2025 count of countries adopting EU-style AI rules, and no baseline to measure 'increasingly'.
The CEPA study dates from April 2025; later 2025 adoptions (e.g., Vietnam) are only partly covered.
